summary: This article explains how a plastic bottle is made from oil, where it goes after use, why plastic lasts so long, and how reducing, reusing, and recycling help.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “The Journey of a Plastic Bottle” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: a small, hard ball or bead of a material
a large area where trash is buried under the ground
to slowly break down into tiny parts, as dead plants do

challengeTerms.def: oil that is found underground and used to make fuel and many materials
a material made of very long chains of small, repeating molecules
able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that recycling is the best way to solve the problem of plastic waste? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why plastic bottles can be a problem for the environment.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review pellet, landfill, and decompose, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use petroleum, polymer, and durable in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
